correctness.rationale: An exact conflict graph for every disjoint pair of corner alphabets A,B partitions all eligible 3-by-3 matrices into abq^2 complete bipartite components K_(bq^4,aq^4) and ab(q-a-b)q^6 isolated vertices. This proves fixed-A/B capacity and, after a strict integer maximization, all-q capacity and the complete equality description. All binary matrices and their overlap conflicts were enumerated; an independent binary integer-program optimum and q=2,3,4 component counts agree. Computation is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Chee et al. give one-dimensional constructions, Blackburn gives the exact one-dimensional length-three optimum, and Barcucci et al. give diagonal lifts to square matrices. These imply the presented lower bound, but do not establish its two-dimensional upper bound or enumerate equality cases among arbitrary matrices. The proof shows 28 binary optimal codebooks are not complete off-diagonal lifts, demonstrating why direct transfer from one-dimensional codes is insufficient. Targeted published-index and primary-source comparisons found no dominating matrix theorem; priority remains qualified by inaccessible/unindexed sources.
residual_risks: Equivalent graph-theoretic classification or numeric table may be unindexed under a different term.
The related arxiv:1601.07723 full text was not accessed, so its possible incidental discussion of weaker diagonal overlaps is not ruled out.
No independent review has assessed historical originality.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial square dimension for diagonal two-dimensional synchronization codes is solved exactly for every alphabet, not just via a construction. Equality rigidity for q>=3 contrasts with 28 non-lift binary maxima. This gives the exact optimal dictionary size and labeled number of attainable designs and clarifies when one-dimensional lifts capture every optimum. The 2015 two-dimensional work only supplied nonexpandable families, leaving sharpness for arbitrary matrices undetermined.
